flashcard_questions.q: Which political document does Old Major’s speech mirror?
Which rhetorical appeal does Old Major use by citing his long life?
Which tricolon does Old Major use to describe the animals’ existence?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Our lives are miserable, laborious, and short.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which appeal to logic identifies Man as the source of animal suffering?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Man is the only creature that consumes without producing.’

flashcard_questions.q: What is logos as a rhetorical appeal?
flashcard_questions.a: An appeal to logic backed by reasoning and evidence.

flashcard_questions.q: Which repeated pair of statements splits the world into two sides?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘All men are enemies. All animals are comrades.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which song closes Old Major’s speech and becomes the revolutionary anthem?
What actually triggers the rebellion in Chapter Two?
flashcard_questions.a: Jones forgets to feed the animals.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Russian revolution does that food-shortage trigger mirror?
Which name do the pigs give Old Major’s ideas as a system?
Which two words were later added to the commandment about killing?
Which food disappears at the end of Chapter Two?
Which grammatical choice hides who took it?
What does Squealer’s ability to ‘turn black into white’ mean?
flashcard_questions.a: He can make lies seem like truth.

flashcard_questions.q: Which invented place does Moses the raven preach about?

notes: 15 cards: 4 quotation-recall fronts (the tricolon, the logos line, the two-sides repetition, ‘Beasts of England’), 3 technique-to-effect (ethos, the passive voice, ‘turn black into white’), 4 plot-detail cards (the trigger, Animalism, the milk, Sugarcandy Mountain), 2 context parallels (Communist Manifesto, February Revolution), 1 commandment change (‘without cause’), 1 term-to-definition (logos). ‘Rhetoric’, ‘pathos’ and ‘utopian’ dropped — four rhetorical-appeal definitions in one deck interfere badly, so ethos is tested by example and logos by definition. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
